a: Central dogma: DNA → RNA → protein (with known exceptions).
The genetic code maps codons to amino acids and stop signals.
Silent mutations change DNA but not the amino acid.
Missense mutations change one amino acid.
Nonsense mutations create a premature stop codon.
Directional, stabilizing, and disruptive selection shift trait distributions differently.
Genetic drift is random change in allele frequencies.
Gene flow is movement of alleles between populations.
Bottlenecks reduce genetic variation after population crashes.
Founder effects occur when a small group starts a new population.
